xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5199: Polyrepo workspaces: work agent start refused as dirty because the wrapper repo doesn't ignore Overdeck's own sync files

plan.title: Polyrepo workspaces: work agent start refused as dirty because the wrapper repo doesn't ignore Overdeck's own sync files
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On polyrepo projects (MYN) the work agent start is refused with WORKSPACE_DIRTY after planning, and nothing retries it. The wrapper repo at the workspace root has a .gitignore that lists the sub-repo dirs, .overdeck/, .devcontainer/ and dev, but none of the files Overdeck itself writes there (.claude/ from skills merge, template copy_dirs, settings/mcp copy and caveman; .mcp.json from the agent template; .hume-config from Hume setup; .env from env.template). The start gate in spawn-issue.ts accepts only .pan/, .overdeck/ and .husky/_/, so `?? .claude/...`, `?? .mcp.json` and `?? .hume-config` refuse every start. Eleven MYN issues hit this; MIN-1141 has been stuck since 2026-11-06.
narratives.Proposal: Add one shared leaf module (src/lib/workspace-sync-paths.ts) holding the project .gitignore entries (moved from ensurePanGitignore) and the workspace-root sync entries (.claude/, .mcp.json, .hume-config, .env), plus an isOverdeckWorkspaceSyncPath predicate. Extract the polyrepo .gitignore helpers from create.ts into src/lib/workspace-manager/polyrepo-gitignore.ts, make ensurePolyrepoWorkspaceGitignore write the shared entries, and add healPolyrepoWorkspaceGitignoreAsync, which ensures and commits the wrapper .gitignore and restores the original file if the commit fails. spawnIssueAgentForRoute calls the heal before the dirty check for local polyrepo workspaces. In polyrepo wrappers only, the start gate (isOnlyOverdeckRuntimeWorkspaceChanges with { polyrepoWrapper: true }) also accepts untracked (??) sync paths through a new status-aware porcelain parser; the heal commit is limited to the .gitignore path; while tracked edits to those paths and every other path stay refused. Docs and a changelog entry describe the behaviour. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-5199.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No automatic retry of starts refused before this fix (MIN-1141 and the other ten); operators run `pan start <issue>` once.
- No change to any monorepo or project .gitignore: ensurePanGitignore output stays byte-identical.
- No widening of isOverdeckWorkspaceRuntimePath or isOverdeckOwnedOnlyStatus; the pan done preflight and merge-ops gates are unchanged.
- No discovery of per-project agent.template_dir *.template targets beyond .mcp.json.
- No start-gate tolerance for tracked or staged changes to sync paths, and none at all for monorepo workspaces.
- No change to where or how Overdeck writes sync files (skills merge, settings copy, caveman, templates, Hume, env).

autoDecisions.summary: One shared leaf module src/lib/workspace-sync-paths.ts holds OVERDECK_PROJECT_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES (moved verbatim from ensurePanGitignore) and OVERDECK_WORKSPACE_ROOT_SYNC_ENTRIES = ['.claude/', '.mcp.json', '.hume-config', '.env'].
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires reusing ensurePanGitignore's list with no second copy, but that list only covers .claude/skills/; a second constant in the same module covers the verified writers without changing project .gitignore output. A leaf with no imports keeps lint:circular green for state-plane, migration and the dashboard route.

autoDecisions.summary: The wrapper .gitignore ignores .claude/ as a whole, while the project list stays .claude/skills/ only.
autoDecisions.rationale: The wrapper is an Overdeck-created scaffold with no remote; every file under its .claude/ is Overdeck output. A project repo can legitimately track parts of .claude/.

autoDecisions.summary: The start gate accepts sync paths only as untracked (??) entries and only in a polyrepo wrapper (isOnlyOverdeckRuntimeWorkspaceChanges(porcelain, { polyrepoWrapper })); monorepo starts are unchanged.
autoDecisions.rationale: In a monorepo, untracked .claude/agents/*.md or .mcp.json can be team-owned work (configuration/meta-repos.mdx), so it must stay refused; inside the wrapper (an Overdeck scaffold with no code) every such file has a verified Overdeck writer. Plan critic round 1 finding.

autoDecisions.summary: Heal runs in spawnIssueAgentForRoute before the dirty check, for local polyrepo workspaces whose wrapper has a .git.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every start path (pan start, dashboard, MCP start_issue, planning auto-handoff, machine work) goes through spawnIssueAgentForRoute; createWorkspace already runs the ensure on its resume path.

autoDecisions.summary: The heal runs only on a tracked, clean wrapper .gitignore, and a failed commit restores .gitignore from HEAD (index and working tree).
autoDecisions.rationale: Leaving ` M .gitignore` would make the gate refuse for a new reason. Restoring from HEAD stays correct when two starts heal at once, because claimAgentStart runs only after the dirty gate. The clean precondition means an uncommitted .gitignore edit is never overwritten.

autoDecisions.summary: .env is included in the sync entries even though the issue names only .mcp.json and .hume-config.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for every path Overdeck writes into a workspace root; create.ts writes .env from workspace.env.template, which would block a polyrepo start the same way.

autoDecisions.summary: Static sync list; no per-project *.template target discovery.
autoDecisions.rationale: The start gate is a pure function over porcelain text and the issue requires one shared list for both uses; .mcp.json is the only root template target in the only live polyrepo project.

autoDecisions.summary: ensurePolyrepoWorkspaceGitignore and commitPolyrepoWorkspaceGitignoreAsync move into src/lib/workspace-manager/polyrepo-gitignore.ts, re-exported from create.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: The route must import the heal without pulling create.ts's DNS/tunnel/Hume/Docker/workspace-row imports; spawn-issue.ts is at 918 of 1000 lines, so the route change stays one guarded call.

autoDecisions.summary: commitPolyrepoWorkspaceGitignoreAsync checks and commits only the .gitignore path (`-- .gitignore`).
autoDecisions.rationale: The heal must never commit an unrelated staged file and hide it from the dirty gate. Plan critic round 1 finding.

metadata.acJustification: Six ACs, one per real-git test case: the heal's safety depends on each failure mode (blocked commit, staged unrelated file, dirty .gitignore, no .git, re-run) being pinned separately.

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-4. First scope commitPolyrepoWorkspaceGitignoreAsync to the one path: `git diff --cached --quiet -- .gitignore` and `git commit -m "chore(workspace): add polyrepo scaffold .gitignore" -- .gitignore`, so any other staged entry stays staged and uncommitted (createWorkspace uses the same helper; the change is correct there too). Then export interface PolyrepoGitignoreHealResult { added: string[]; committed: boolean; warning: string | null } and async healPolyrepoWorkspaceGitignoreAsync(workspacePath, repos). Steps: (1) return the no-op result { added: [], committed: false, warning: null } when join(workspacePath, '.git') does not exist; (2) return the no-op result unless `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- .gitignore` succeeds and `git status --porcelain -- .gitignore` prints nothing; (3) run ensurePolyrepoWorkspaceGitignore and return no-op when added is empty; (4) call commitPolyrepoWorkspaceGitignoreAsync; (5) `git status --porcelain -- .gitignore` empty means committed:true; (6) otherwise run `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- .gitignore` and return committed:false with the commit message or 'wrapper .gitignore commit did not land' as warning (race-safe: claimAgentStart runs after the gate); (7) try/catch so it never throws; after a throw following step 3 run the step-6 restore best effort and return { added: [], committed: false, warning: err.message }. Only async child-process calls. Add src/lib/workspace-manager/__tests__/polyrepo-gitignore-heal.test.ts with a real git repo in mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), ...)), GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env, `git config core.hooksPath .git/hooks`, and no child_process mock, covering the six PRD cases (commit + clean tree; second run no-op; failing pre-commit hook restores from HEAD; no .git; unrelated staged notes.txt stays staged and out of the commit; uncommitted .gitignore edit left alone). The test must not import the dashboard route.

items.title: Given a git wrapper with a MIN-1141-shaped committed .gitignore and untracked .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json and .hume-config, when the heal runs, then it returns committed:true and `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` produces empty output with two commits in git log
When the heal runs a second time on the healed wrapper, then it returns added:[] and committed:false and creates no third commit

Given a pre-commit hook that exits 1, when the heal runs, then it returns committed:false with a non-null warning, the .gitignore content equals the HEAD content, and `git status --porcelain -- .gitignore` produces empty output
Given a plain directory without .git, when the heal runs, then it returns { added: [], committed: false, warning: null } and creates no .gitignore

Given a wrapper with `notes.txt` staged, when the heal runs, then it commits only .gitignore (`git show --name-only --format= HEAD` lists only .gitignore) and `git status --porcelain` still shows `A  notes.txt`
Given a committed .gitignore with an uncommitted local edit, when the heal runs, then it returns the no-op result and preserves the edited file content byte for byte
